notes: 20-item bank. CAPS mix: 5 L1 / 8 L2 / 7 L3. Graphs given as point tables + descriptive captions (no image). Topics: dependent vs independent, discrete vs continuous, plain-language description.

stimulus.inline:
**Graph A** — Distance travelled (km, vertical axis) over Time (hours, horizontal axis):

| Time (h) | Distance (km) |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 60 |
| 2 | 120 |
| 3 | 180 |

items.question: What is the independent variable in Graph A?
workingSteps: The independent variable is plotted on the horizontal axis and is the one we control.

stimulus.inline:
**Graph A** — Distance travelled (km, vertical axis) over Time (hours, horizontal axis):

| Time (h) | Distance (km) |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 60 |
| 2 | 120 |
| 3 | 180 |

items.question: What is the dependent variable in Graph A?
workingSteps: The dependent variable is on the vertical axis and depends on time.

stimulus.inline: Discrete data consists of separate, countable values (number of learners). Continuous data is measured on a scale (height, mass, temperature).

items.question: Which of these is continuous data?
options: Number of learners in a class
Number of cars in a parking lot
workingSteps: Height is measured (any value within a range), so it's continuous. The others are counted.

stimulus.inline: Discrete = countable separate values. Continuous = measured on a scale.

items.question: Which of these is discrete data?
workingSteps: Goals can only be whole counted values — discrete.

stimulus.inline: **Story-graph B** — A learner's height (cm, vertical axis) plotted against age (years, horizontal axis) shows steady growth from 100 cm at age 5 to 175 cm at age 18.

items.question: Which variable is independent?
workingSteps: Age progresses on its own; height depends on age.

stimulus.inline: **Story-graph C** — A taxi driver's earnings (R, vertical) over a 12-hour shift (hours, horizontal). Earnings rise steadily from R0 at 06:00 to R600 by 10:00, then stay flat (lunch break) until 12:00, then rise again to R1 200 by 18:00.

items.question: What does the FLAT section between 10:00 and 12:00 represent?
options: He earned more money very quickly.
He was not earning during those hours (e.g. lunch break).
items.expectedAnswer: He was not earning during those hours (e.g. lunch break).
workingSteps: A flat section means the y-value (earnings) is not changing over time — no new earnings.

stimulus.inline: **Story-graph D** — A water tank's level (L, vertical) over time (minutes, horizontal). The graph DESCENDS from 200 L at 0 min down to 0 L at 40 min.

items.question: In plain language, describe what the graph shows.
options: The tank is filling at a steady rate.
The tank is emptying at a steady rate.
The tank's level is staying constant.
items.expectedAnswer: The tank is emptying at a steady rate.
workingSteps: A descending straight line means y (litres) decreases at a constant rate as x (time) increases.

stimulus.inline:
**Story-graph E** — Number of learners absent each day in a school week:

| Day | Absent |
|---|---|
| Mon | 12 |
| Tue | 8 |
| Wed | 5 |
| Thu | 6 |
| Fri | 15 |

items.question: Is this DISCRETE or CONTINUOUS data?
workingSteps: Number of learners is a count — only whole values — discrete.

stimulus.inline: **Story-graph F** — Temperature in Joburg (°C, vertical) over 24 hours (hour, horizontal). Cool overnight (~10 °C), rises to peak (~26 °C) at 14:00, drops back.

items.question: Which variable is dependent?
workingSteps: Temperature changes as a function of time — temperature depends on time.

stimulus.inline: **Story-graph F** — Temperature in Joburg (°C, vertical) over 24 hours (hour, horizontal). Cool overnight (~10 °C), rises to peak (~26 °C) at 14:00, drops back.

items.question: At approximately what time of day is the temperature highest?
workingSteps: The peak is described as occurring at 14:00.

stimulus.inline: **Graph G** — Mr Mokoena's car odometer reading (km, vertical) versus weeks (horizontal). Reading rose from 48 000 km in week 1 to 51 200 km in week 8.

items.question: Calculate the average distance driven per week.
workingSteps: Change in km = 51 200 − 48 000 = 3 200 km.
Change in weeks = 8 − 1 = 7.
Average = 3 200 ÷ 7 ≈ 457 km/week.
(Or read 8 weeks of driving as 3 200 ÷ 8 = 400 km/week — accept either method.)

stimulus.inline: **Story-graph H** — Distance from home (km, vertical) as a learner walks from home to school over time (minutes, horizontal). The line goes UP from 0 km at 0 min to 2 km at 20 min, then comes back DOWN to 0 km at 40 min.

items.question: What story does this graph tell?
options: Learner walks steadily to school and then home again.
Learner stays at home all day.
Learner runs in circles around the house.
items.expectedAnswer: Learner walks steadily to school and then home again.
workingSteps: Going up = moving away. Coming down = returning. Same distance up and back is a round trip.

stimulus.inline:
**Sales-graph J** — Pies sold per day at a stall over the first 5 days of trading:

| Day | Pies sold |
|---|---|
| 1 | 25 |
| 2 | 32 |
| 3 | 38 |
| 4 | 41 |
| 5 | 47 |

items.question: Is the trend INCREASING, DECREASING, or CONSTANT?
workingSteps: Each day's value is larger than the previous — increasing trend.

stimulus.inline: **Graph K** — Cooldrink remaining in a 2 L bottle (litres, vertical) over time during a party (hours, horizontal). Starts at 2,0 L. After 1 hour: 1,4 L. After 2 hours: 0,8 L. After 3 hours: 0,2 L.

items.question: What is the average rate of consumption per hour?
workingSteps: Total drunk = 2,0 − 0,2 = 1,8 L over 3 hours.

stimulus.inline: **Story-graph L** — A jogger's heart rate (bpm, vertical) over a 30-minute run (minutes, horizontal). Starts at 70 bpm, rises to 160 bpm by 10 min, stays at 160 bpm until 20 min, then drops to 90 bpm by 30 min.

items.question: What is happening between minute 10 and minute 20?
options: Heart rate is steady (jogger is running at constant effort).
Heart rate is falling (jogger is resting).
items.expectedAnswer: Heart rate is steady (jogger is running at constant effort).
workingSteps: A flat section means the dependent variable is not changing.

stimulus.inline: **Graph M** — Daily egg sales (vertical) by week of the year (horizontal). The line goes UP from January to June, then DOWN again to December, mirror-image around June.

items.question: Describe this pattern in plain language.
options: Peaks mid-year, lower at the start and end (seasonal pattern).
items.expectedAnswer: Peaks mid-year, lower at the start and end (seasonal pattern).
workingSteps: Up then down with the peak in the middle is a seasonal/cyclic pattern.

stimulus.inline:
Three datasets:

- (i) Mass of newborn babies in a maternity ward.
- (ii) Number of times a learner is late this term.
- (iii) Daily rainfall in mm at OR Tambo Airport.

items.question: Which datasets are continuous?
workingSteps: Mass is measured — continuous.
Number of times late is counted — discrete.
Rainfall is measured — continuous.

stimulus.inline: **Story-graph N** — A geyser's water temperature (°C, vertical) over time (hours, horizontal) after switching on. Starts at 20 °C, rises QUICKLY at first to 50 °C in 1 hour, then SLOWS, reaching 60 °C at 2 hours and only 65 °C at 4 hours.

items.question: Which best describes how the temperature changes over the 4 hours?
options: Linear — temperature rises by the same amount each hour.
Rising and then levelling off (heating slows as temperature approaches max).
items.expectedAnswer: Rising and then levelling off (heating slows as temperature approaches max).
workingSteps: Hour 0–1: rise of 30 °C.
Hour 1–2: rise of 10 °C.
Hour 2–4: rise of only 5 °C total.
Rate of rise decreases — graph levels off.

stimulus.inline: **Sales-graph P** — Ice-cream sales (R per week, vertical) vs week of year (horizontal). The dependent variable peaks in summer (week 1 = January) and is lowest in winter (week 28 ≈ July).

items.question: What does the relationship between ice-cream sales and time of year suggest is the REAL underlying driver?
workingSteps: Sales rise when it's hot (summer) and fall when it's cold (winter) — temperature is the driver, time of year is the proxy.

stimulus.inline: **Graph Q** — Total marks (vertical) for a Maths Lit class plotted against hours studied per week (horizontal). The line rises steeply from 0 to 5 hours, then continues to rise but more gently to 15 hours.

items.question: What story does this graph tell?
options: Studying more always helps the same amount per hour.
Studying more helps, but the extra benefit shrinks per additional hour.
items.expectedAnswer: Studying more helps, but the extra benefit shrinks per additional hour.
workingSteps: Steep at first, gentler later means each extra hour adds fewer marks — diminishing returns.

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_GRAPH_DIRECTION: Reads a rising graph as falling (or vice versa).
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_GRAPH_SHAPE_READ: Misinterprets the shape of a graph (e.g. ignores flat sections).
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_GRAPH_PEAK_READ: Reads off the wrong x-value for a peak or minimum.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_SLOPE_INTERPRETATION: Misinterprets the slope (rate of change) of a line.
